concept: Solana staking, liquid staking and restaking
summary: Native SOL staking delegates stake accounts to validators (commission, epoch-boundary warmup and cooldown), liquid staking tokens such as JitoSOL, mSOL, bSOL, JupSOL and Sanctum's INF wrap that stake as reward-bearing exchange-rate tokens, and restaking (Jito (Re)staking, Solayer; EigenLayer and ETH LRTs for contrast) re-uses staked assets to secure further services. Drawn from 222 research sources across definitions, mechanisms, parameters, measures, problems and comparisons. Evidence status: research claims ungated (v4 evidence gate not passed); treat as leads with cited sources.

facts.text: INF is the pool token of Sanctum's Infinity, a shared liquidity pool of LSTs. Infinity prices each LST at its intrinsic SOL value, which a per-LST 'SOL value calculator' program reads from the on-chain state of that LST's own stake program (calculators exist for Marinade mSOL, Sanctum LSTs, jitoSOL, bSOL and wSOL). It uses no constant-product or stableswap curve, and Sanctum says swaps have zero price impact. A Flat Fee Pricing Program still charges per-LST input and output fees in basis points plus a 20 bps fee on liquidity withdrawal, and splits fees 90/10 between pool reserves and protocol

A liquid staking token (LST) is a tokenized representation of staked tokens on a proof-of-stake chain that keeps earning staking rewards and stays usable in DeFi. Restaking lets staked tokens or LSTs secure extra protocols for extra rewards, and a liquid restaking token (LRT) makes that restaked position liquid. Lido's ReGOOSE post (May 2024) calls the LST 'a commoditized software offering' and says an LRT is 'closer to ETH-denominated mutual funds or tokenized deposits in an Ethereum lending market', so LRTs are less likely to gain deep liquidity and network effects.

INF is a reward-bearing (not rebasing) token for Sanctum's Infinity pool, a basket of LSTs. Its yield is the weighted average staking yield of the LSTs held plus swap fees earned by routing trades between them.

An LST is a token for staked assets on a proof-of-stake chain that keeps earning staking rewards while staying usable in DeFi. An LRT is a token that makes a restaked position (staked tokens, LSTs, or native BTC tokens securing extra protocols) liquid. Lido's ReGOOSE post frames LRTs as the riskier, actively managed product and the LST as the commoditized one.

Among validators that pass the gates, the Steward score is a packed u64 compared lexicographically. Tier 1 is the highest inflation commission over 30 epochs (lower wins). Tier 2 is the ceiling-averaged MEV commission over valid epochs (lower wins; 10000 bps if there are none). Tier 3 is validator age in epochs with vote credits. Tier 4 is the vote-credit ratio. A 1-point inflation commission difference outranks any MEV commission, age or performance difference. Before Deactivate is called, Withdraw treats the whole delegation as staked, even while it is still warming up. After the deactivation epoch begins, only lamports above the remaining effective stake plus the rent-exempt reserve can leave. Withdrawing the full balance of an account that still has staked lamports fails with InsufficientFunds, and an unexpired Lockup fails with LockupInForce unless the custodian signs.

One address, 5eosrve6LktMZgVNszYzebgmmC7BjLK8NoWyRQtcmGTF, is the upgrade authority of both Jito programs (read with mainnet JSON-RPC getAccountInfo on 2026-11-06). Solayer's current docs describe sSOL as a liquid staking token and a 'universal liquidity layer', not as a restaking receipt. A user converts SOL or an LST to sSOL, and the pool stakes with Solayer's own validator ('Mega Validator'). A holder can then delegate sSOL to an endoAVS, which mints a wrapper token as proof of stake. An endoAVS is a Solana dApp that gains a higher chance of block space and transaction inclusion through stake-weighted quality of service (swQoS). The docs say 'each unit of sSOL represents a unit of blockspace'. Letting dApps pick the validators is described as future wo

MIP-19 (posted 2025-12-16, Realms vote live 2025-12-22) proposed that SAM winners bid for stake priority, that Marinade undelegates part of the stake of any validator whose bond falls below the required level, that the per-validator cap rise from 4% to up to 15% of TVL, and that MNDE Enhanced Stake be removed. The result of the vote was not found.

On 2025-06-24 Marinade said it had manually blocklisted 73 validators for sandwiching about three months earlier, would slash the bonds of malicious validators to cover re-delegation fees, and expected the removals to cost about 0.9 percentage points of APY on average. It pointed to Marinade Select (30+ curated validators) as a sandwiching-free option. SolanaFloor is a Jito Network subsidiary, which matters because Jito is part of this debate.

Sanctum Infinity (INF) is a multi-LST pool that holds a basket of LSTs plus a buffer of unstaked SOL, and prices every swap from each LST's on-chain rate. Each asset has an inputFee and an outputFee in bps, and the swap fee is their sum. In the March 2024 design the fee was flat and did not grow with size. The pool manager raises fees on the side the pool is short of, to attract rebalancing swaps. Each epoch INF unstakes part of its holdings to restock its liquid SOL. INF holders earn the basket's staking yield plus swap fees. This is Sanctum's description of its own design.

Sanctum's main revenue is white-label LSTs: partners such as Jupiter, Drift and Bybit launch their own LST, and Sanctum charges an AUM fee that it splits 50/50 with the partner (Sanctum co-founder FP Lee, 2025-09-12). JupSOL matches this: its 5% epoch fee splits 2.5% to Sanctum and 2.5% to the Jupiter DAO treasury. Sanctum says it has no revenue-share deal with Binance's bnSOL but still earns fees when bnSOL trades through its liquidity layer. Jupiter's FAQ calls the Sanctum share an infrastructure fee.

Most stake sits with low-fee validators, but a large block charges everything. Solana Compass's stake-weighted bands (2026-10-30) put inflation commission at 0% for 31% of staked SOL, 1-5% for 25%, 6-10% for 20%, 11-99% for 0% and 100% for 24%. MEV commission is 0% for 34%, 1-5% for 6%, 6-10% for 28%, 11-99% for 3% and 100% for 29%. So about 29% of staked SOL passes no tips to delegators. Compass says most validators at 100% inflation commission are private validators run by exchanges and custodians. Withdraw is limited to lamports above the account's still-staked amount plus its rent reserve. If the stake has not been deactivated, the staked amount is the full delegation, so nothing delegated can be withdrawn during warmup. Once the current epoch is at or after deactivation_epoch, the staked amount is the remaining effective stake, so lamports that already cooled can be withdrawn in part during a multi-epoch cooldown. Withdrawing the entire balance (closing the account) needs a staked amount of zero. The withdraw authority must sign. A lockup in force blocks withdrawal unless the lockup c

If activation_epoch equals deactivation_epoch, stake_and_activating returns (0, 0): a stake delegated and then deactivated within one epoch has no stake at all, so there is no cooldown to wait for and the lamports are withdrawable at once. Deactivating a stake that is still partway through warmup cools only the part that had become effective.

Jito Liquid Staking TVL was about $972.24M on 2026-11-02 per DefiLlama (down 21.4% over 30 days, ranked #8 among liquid staking protocols there). JIP-39 (posted 2026-08-26) separately states JitoSOL TVL is down about 50% from its all-time high. Dollar TVL moves with SOL price, so part of the drop may not be outflow.

Pool fees are now the larger part of Jito's protocol revenue. Blockworks Advisory's Q2 2026 report puts protocol revenue at $1.28M, of which $733K (57%) came from staking epoch and withdrawal fees and $539K (42%) from MEV-tip fees; BAM subsidies cost $1.2M that quarter. The pool figure is the same order as the on-chain fee: a 4% epoch fee on about 5.9% gross yield on about 10M SOL is roughly 6,000 SOL a quarter, plus 0.1% withdrawal fees, or about $0.5-0.7M at the roughly $73-82 per SOL that DefiLlama's series implies for Q2 (researcher's estimate).

Fee layers in MEV distribution are not reconciled. The FAQ says TipRouter pays 97% of MEV to validators and stakers with a 3% protocol fee, and charges 1.5% on priority-fee distributions (split 5% LST vault operators, 5% JTO vault operators, 90% DAO). Blockworks' filing says tokenholders govern 6% of Jito tips plus the 4% JitoSOL fee. No source read here explains how the 3% and the 6% relate.

For native stake, the unstake delay is the time from Deactivate to the next epoch boundary, plus extra epochs only if the 9% cooldown cap binds. That is 0 to one epoch: 0 to 24 h at the nominal 200 ms slot time (about 0 to 26 h measured on 2026-11-06), against 0 to 48 h before SIMD-0525. The stake program counts epochs, not clock time, and SIMD-0525 does not mention warmup or cooldown, so the wall-clock delay shrank without a stake program change (inference). Activation follows the same boundary logic: stake delegated in epoch N becomes effective in N+1.

Chaos Labs' post-Pectra scenarios for Lido wstETH cover the consensus layer only, not AVS slashing. An isolated slashing costs about 0% of Lido stake (22.48 ETH). A majority consensus-client bug with a 13-day inactivity leak (about 30% of Lido operators on the faulty client) costs about 6.77% (634,648 ETH), with about $350M of Aave liquidations and $233K of bad debt. A minority-client bug with slashing costs about 15%, with $824M of liquidations and $48M of bad debt. Lido's slashing insurance fund held about 6,500 stETH at the time.

Solayer's docs claim that stakers using its validator pay 0% commission and receive 100% of MEV, and they quote '10+% APY historical returns' for the sSOL pool. The docs describe the validator as a dedicated-hardware node in Ashburn, Virginia. These are vendor statements, and the sources read contain no independent check.

The minimum delegation on mainnet-beta is 1 SOL (1,000,000,000 lamports). SIMD-0490 raised it from 1 lamport as part of the v5 stake program, news reports it live on 2026-06-18, stake program 5.1.0 hard-codes 1 SOL, and getStakeMinimumDelegation returned 1000000000 on 2026-11-06. News coverage says the rule covers new stake accounts only and leaves existing delegations unchanged; SIMD-0490 says accounts under 1 SOL held about 0.02% of active stake.

DeactivateDelinquentStake lets anyone deactivate stake delegated to a vote account that has never voted or has not voted in the last 5 epochs (MINIMUM_DELINQUENT_EPOCHS_FOR_DEACTIVATION). The caller also passes a reference vote account with acceptable recent epoch credits; otherwise the instruction fails with InsufficientReferenceVotes. The reference guards against a chain warped ahead by 5 epochs. The v1.14 post says '5 epochs; about 15 days'. At the measured 25.7 hour epoch, 5 epochs is about 5.4 days, so windows counted in epochs now cover less wall-clock time.

The Steward program (part of StakeNet) is an Anchor program that holds the staking authority of the SPL stake pool, scores validators from on-chain Validator History data, keeps target stake on the winners, and re-evaluates the set on a fixed cadence. Its core operations are permissionless, so any cranker can run them, and its parameters are set through Jito DAO governance.

ChaosLabs modelled consensus-layer penalties for Lido wstETH after Pectra. Single-operator slashing or downtime costs about 0% of Lido stake (22.48 ETH for an ~8,192 ETH isolated slashing). A majority consensus-client bug with a 13-day inactivity leak costs about 6.77% (634,648 ETH), roughly $350M of Aave liquidations and about $233K of bad debt. A minority-client bug with slashing costs about 15%. The model covers LSTs only, not AVS slashing.

Chaos Labs modelled consensus-layer penalties for Lido's wstETH after Pectra, assuming 34M ETH staked and no operator above about 2.7% of Lido stake. Isolated operator slashing of about 8,192 ETH costs 22.48 ETH (about 0% of Lido stake). A minority-client bug with slashing costs 1,409,226.8 ETH (about 15%), $824M of liquidations and $48M of bad debt. The model covers LSTs only, not AVS slashing.

Jito's docs still treat an epoch as about 2-3 days: the glossary says so, and the FAQ gives 'up to 1 epoch (~2-3 days max)' for direct unstaking and 'approximately 20-30 days' for a 10-epoch Steward cycle. The chain now runs shorter epochs. Epoch 1051 began 2026-10-06 22:14 UTC and epoch 1078 began 2026-11-05 11:54 UTC, so 27 epochs took 29.6 days, about 1.1 days each (about 0.22 s per slot). JIP-39 itself notes slot times compressing from 350ms toward 200ms and describes a 20-day Steward cycle. The unstake wait and the cycle are shorter in wall-clock time than the docs say.

If a staker calls Deactivate in epoch N, the whole stake stays effective during N and keeps earning for N; the status is 'deactivating' with all of it still effective. Cooldown applies from N+1. When the cluster-wide deactivating stake in N is within the 9% allowance, the account is fully inactive at the start of N+1 and Withdraw can take everything except the rent-exempt reserve. Otherwise the remainder cools down pro rata over later epochs and keeps earning on the part still effective.

Solayer's restaking is now one product line among several. Its docs index groups content under Solayer Chain (InfiniSVM), sSOL, sUSD, Solayer Pay and LAYER staking, with no page titled restaking or slashing, and DefiLlama lists the Solayer parent with Solayer Restaking, Solayer USD and Solayer Card as separate protocols.

Geographic weighting has been proposed but not adopted. A June 2025 draft would put 20% of the pool on 200 validators more than 30 degrees of longitude from the stake centre of mass, at an estimated 5-15 bp yield cost, using an ipinfo.io geo-IP oracle; a Jito commenter replied that proof of location is really hard. On 2025-09-23 the JIP-25 lead said geo-spatial inputs add subjectivity and off-chain permissioning that run against permissionless design. The README scoring tiers contain no geographic input.

Thin pools hit long-tail LSTs hardest. Sanctum says it supports over 1,300 LSTs and that a well-supported LST can trade within a fraction of a percent of fair value while a smaller LST with limited DEX liquidity and no shared liquidity layer can see much wider spreads in volatile periods. Sanctum says price impact on shallow-reserve LSTs can spike even at modest sizes, and that delayed unstake avoids pool liquidity entirely. This is a vendor statement.

An epoch is 432,000 slots (Chorus One; confirmed by a live getEpochSchedule call on mainnet on 2026-11-06: slotsPerEpoch 432000, epoch 1078). Wall-clock length is quoted as about 2-3 days (Chorus One) or about 2 days (stake.fish). The mainnet RPC reported epoch 1078 at slot index 389193 when checked.

EigenLayer TVL has fallen roughly 70-75% from its 2025 level. The Block reported an all-time high of $20.1B in early June 2024. DefiLlama figures give $19.00B on 2025-10-04 (Sevim and Torres) and $22.06B in August 2025 (Blockhead), then $5.10B in late September 2026 (Blockhead) and $5.72B on 2026-11-06 (DefiLlama API). These are USD values, and ETH/USD fell 47% in H1 2026 (Lido), so part of the drop is price.

Solayer's drop was abrupt and Jito's gradual. Solayer lost 60% of TVL in 18 days ($352.6M on 2025-02-11 to $141.1M on 2025-03-01, with SOL held falling from 1.40M to 0.74M); 2025-02-11 is also the date of Binance Research's LAYER report, which gives listing-time token figures. Jito Restaking fell from $395.9M on 2025-07-01 to $198.8M on 2025-08-01 and $54.0M by 2025-12-01. No source read attributes either fall to a cause.

Pectra (Electra) changed Ethereum consensus-layer slashing. The consensus spec sets MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA at 2,048 ETH, MIN_ACTIVATION_BALANCE at 32 ETH and MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ELECTRA at 4,096. EIP-7251 describes the old initial penalty as 1/32 of effective balance, and LlamaRisk and Chaos Labs both report it fell to 1/4096.

Marinade sells three SOL products. mSOL is the liquid staking token, issued by Marinade's own on-chain program. Marinade Native mints no token: the user keeps withdraw authority over the stake account. Marinade Select delegates to a separate vetted validator set. Native and mSOL delegate through the Stake Auction Marketplace (SAM), where validators bid for stake.

bSOL (BlazeStake / SolBlaze) uses the official Solana Labs SPL stake-pool program. Its docs claim 200+ validators, the largest validator set of any Solana stake pool, and a Custom Liquid Staking feature that lets users direct stake to chosen validators. Instant unstake draws on pool reserves at a higher fee than delayed unstake.

mSOL, bSOL, JupSOL and INF are all reward-bearing exchange-rate tokens, not rebasing tokens: the holder's token balance stays fixed and each token redeems for more SOL as staking rewards accrue. Helius noted in Feb 2024 that Solana had no rebasing LSTs. Marinade documents the mSOL price as total_staked / tokens_minted, recalculated each epoch. Jupiter documents JupSOL the same way, so 1 SOL deposited today buys less than 1 JupSOL. Sanctum states that INF is reward-bearing, not rebasing. BlazeStake says bSOL is designed to rise against SOL every epoch.
Marinade's help article says that for mSOL a delayed-unstake request made in the last 2 hours of an epoch is pushed back one epoch (up to about 2 days); native stake accounts have no cut-off.

Marinade prepares mSOL delayed unstakes about 2 hours before an epoch ends. A request made in that last window misses the preparation and becomes claimable one epoch later, at the start of the epoch after next. Marinade also says its bot must run at each epoch start to update the mSOL price, so it advises starting a delayed unstake a few hours into the epoch and before the last 2 hours. Native stake accounts have no such cut-off. This settles an earlier doubt: the window is 2 hours, not 4.

At the end of each epoch Infinity compares its SOL reserve with a target. If the reserve is above target, it stakes the excess into Sanctum's top-performing LSTs inside the pool. If the reserve is below target, it unstakes the worst-performing LSTs to refill the reserve. Sanctum's technical docs are the only source for this rule, and the docs are undated.

An SPL stake pool redeems one pool token for total_lamports / pool_token_supply SOL, rounded down: calc_lamports_withdraw_amount in state.rs is pool_tokens * total_lamports / pool_token_supply in integer math. Both totals sit in the StakePool account, and UpdateStakePoolBalance rewrites them from the reserve plus every validator stake record. Rewards therefore enter the redemption rate only when a crank runs the update after an epoch boundary. Marinade's mSOL, a separate program, follows the same pattern: price = total_staked / tokens_minted, recalculated each epoch by a bot.

Infinity does not use a constant-product or stableswap curve. Each LST's exchange rate is read from its stake pool's on-chain state, so Sanctum says trades of any size execute at fair value with zero price impact. This is a vendor claim that no independent source tested.

When an issuer's own frontend is gone, third-party routes can still convert the LST. In the Lido case, a Sanctum team member told DL News that holders could trade stSOL for SOL or other LSTs through Sanctum, Cointelegraph noted users pointing to Sanctum or Jupiter, and a Marinade contributor told SolanaFloor the Marinade app can redelegate any stake account or LST instantly. SolanaFloor is a subsidiary of Jito Network, a Marinade competitor, and the Marinade statement is the contributor's own.

Stake changes happen only at epoch boundaries. A stake account delegates to one vote account. When it is delegated in epoch N, the stake program records activation_epoch = N, and during N the whole amount is 'activating' with nothing effective. When it is deactivated in epoch D, the program records deactivation_epoch = D. The effective, activating and deactivating amounts for any epoch are computed from those two numbers plus the cluster stake history. The four states are inactive, activating, active (effective) and deactivating.

An LST tokenizes staked tokens on a proof-of-stake chain and keeps earning staking rewards while it stays usable in DeFi. An LRT tokenizes a restaked position, where staked tokens or LSTs also secure other protocols for extra rewards. The SoK paper says LRT architecture, token model and peg mechanism match those of LSTs. Kelp's rsETH shows the pattern: users deposit ETH, the protocol routes it through EigenLayer, and users get a tradeable receipt.

In the SPL stake-pool program, withdraw-sol pays from the pool's reserve and fails if the reserve holds too little SOL (normal when the manager has staked all of it). Withdraw-stake always works unless the user's pool-token account is frozen, but it returns an active stake account, so the holder must deactivate it and wait for the epoch boundary. Withdrawal order for stake: preferred validator, any validator, transient, reserve, then removing a validator account.

INF assets under management rose from $298M to over $360M during October 2025, helped by new INF-SOL and INF-USDC vaults on Jupiter Lend. Sanctum's October 2025 update says INF 'stabilizes LST depegs' in stress, but it does not explain the 'epoch 866' post it links to, and no independent source describing an INF incident was found.

The JitoSOL exchange rate equals total pool lamports divided by pool token supply. Epoch rewards raise lamports while supply stays fixed, so holders get no payout or rebase; the rate started at 1:1. In the SPL design the pool charges its epoch fee after validator commissions, by minting pool tokens into the manager's fee account in proportion to earned rewards. Jito's FAQ says the rate could fall in extreme cases (slashing, a stake-pool bug) and notes slashing 'does not really exist right now on Solana'.

An LRT exit stacks several delays. The LRT adds its own buffer or cooldown on top of EigenLayer's 14-day withdrawal delay (ELIP-002; Kiln says it was 7 days before). In 2024 Renzo used hourly-replenished withdrawal buffers and a 3-day cooldown that LlamaRisk said would rise to 7 days once slashing launched. For native restaking, Gauntlet adds that exiting 5,000-10,000 validators on Ethereum takes about 6 days. Gauntlet says both secondary liquidity and redemption capacity are limited when liquidators sell LRT collateral.

The stake program refuses to merge 'transient' stake (activating or deactivating with non-zero effective stake). A stake account holding both active and deactivating stake can never be merged into. This broke the SPL stake pool DecreaseAdditionalValidatorStake instruction (issue #6275, opened 2024-02-20, closed 'not planned' 2025-03-06 before the repo was archived). Neodyme flags the same rule as stopping direct-merge pools (including the single stake pool) from accepting deposits while pool stake is transient.

Moving stake between validators needs cooldown then warmup. A naive sequence costs about 2 epochs (about 4 days) without rewards. Anza adds that only one re-delegation is allowed per epoch. Stake pools avoid the gap by managing transient accounts.

Deactivate on a delegation whose deactivation_epoch is already set fails with StakeError::AlreadyDeactivated. Pool code that removes validators must skip the Deactivate call for accounts that are already deactivating or deactivated, as the SPL stake pool did in PR #5439 (Neodyme change review, 2023-11-14).

The StakeHistory sysvar keeps at most 512 epochs (MAX_ENTRIES = 512), each with effective, activating and deactivating totals. When a warmup or cooldown walk reaches an epoch older than the retained history, the code assumes the stake is fully effective or fully deactivated. The CLI command solana stake-history shows recent entries and solana stake-account shows the delegation details of one account.

The Validator History program keeps up to 512 epochs (about three years) of per-validator data in one ValidatorHistory account: vote credits, commission, MEV commission, client version and type; the ERPC write-up adds total stake and stake rank. The Steward scores validators from this on-chain record. The README dates its audit 2024-01-12.

Native stake has no live slashing. The Anza docs say cooling stake 'continues to earn rewards and be exposed to slashing', and Chorus One (2021) said slashing was not yet activated. The slashing proposal SIMD-0204 (slashable event verification, created 2024-11-26) still had status Review in the SIMD repo on 2026-11-06. The Solana docs state the purpose of the warmup and cooldown cap as preventing large sudden changes in stake across the network, not backing a slashing window.

The Sanctum Reserve is backstop liquidity for last-resort needs, used when neither the Router nor Infinity can serve a request. The user hands the Reserve authority over an active stake account (an LST is first burned to extract its stake account) and receives SOL minus a fee. The Reserve then deactivates that stake at epoch end to refill. The fee is dynamic on the share of SOL left in the Reserve and ranges from 8 to 800 bps. The page says the Reserve held over 600,000 SOL and that retail deposits are closed; it showed 'last updated 11 months ago' when fetched.

JitoSOL's exchange rate is Total Pool Lamports divided by Pool Token Supply (the standard SPL Stake Pool formula). Staking and MEV rewards add lamports while supply stays constant, so the rate rises over time and holders receive no separate payout. The rate started at 1:1. Jito's FAQ says it could fall in extreme cases (slashing, smart-contract bugs).

JitoSOL's exchange rate (SOL per JitoSOL) is Total Pool Lamports divided by Pool Token Supply, the standard SPL stake pool accounting. Staking and MEV rewards add lamports while token supply stays constant, so holders get no payouts and the rate rises instead. It started at 1:1. Jito's docs say it could fall only in extreme cases such as slashing or a stake pool program bug.

mSOL, JupSOL, INF and bSOL are all reward-bearing tokens, not rebasing tokens. A holder's token count stays fixed and each token redeems for more SOL as rewards accrue. Marinade prices mSOL as total staked SOL divided by mSOL minted. Jupiter says the JupSOL/SOL ratio rises over time. Sanctum calls INF reward-bearing, not rebasing. BlazeStake says bSOL is designed to rise against SOL every epoch.

Stake changes take effect only at epoch boundaries. A new delegation sits in 'activating' until the next boundary and earns nothing in the epoch it was confirmed in. Anza states 'A % of the validator's stake is activated on an epoch boundary.'

Only fully inactive lamports can be withdrawn. After `deactivate-stake`, the staker waits for cooldown, then runs `withdraw-stake`. A stake account that has been deactivated and withdrawn is reused only by creating or funding a new delegation. Partial withdrawals are done with split operations.

Merge sorts each account by its status in the current epoch: inactive, activation-epoch (effective 0 but activating), fully active, or transient (effective above 0 together with activating or deactivating stake). Transient stake always fails with StakeError::MergeTransientStake. Allowed pairs are inactive+inactive, inactive+activation-epoch (the destination stays inactive and the source's activation is dropped), activation-epoch+inactive, activation-epoch+activation-epoch, and fully-active+fully-active. A Jito vault withdrawal ticket unlocks only when the current epoch is greater than the unstake epoch plus one (is_withdrawable in vault_staker_withdrawal_ticket.rs). How SAM allocates Marinade stake (docs dated 2026-11-04): each epoch validators bid for delegated stake and are ranked by max_yield (called totalPmpe in code), which equals bid plus inflation and MEV yield after the validator's commissions. Stake is allocated top-down under a last-price (clearing-price) rule: validators above the clearing level pay only enough to deliver the realized yield to stakers. Static bids (CPMPE, cost per 1,000 SOL per epoch) and dynamic commission bids are both paid from a bond. Scoring runs once per epoch and Marinade's bot moves stake toward the target distribution.

Delegate on a stake account with any effective stake fails with TooSoonToRedelegate, except for the same vote account in the epoch where Deactivate was called, which rescinds the deactivation (the account must still hold at least the delegated amount). To change validator, the stake must finish cooldown, then be delegated again and warm up from zero. Inactive accounts, and accounts still in their activation epoch with zero effective stake, can be delegated again immediately. Native Redelegate is disabled: stake program 5.1.0 returns InvalidInstructionData for it.

Across SPL stake pool LSTs, the staker authority can redelegate stake and raise fees (fee increases are capped and take at least one epoch to apply), and the pool program is upgraded by a multisig. Jupiter docs say JupSOL's upgrade authority is an 11-member multisig with a threshold of 6.

Ranking is lexicographic over four tiers: (1) inflation commission, lower first; (2) MEV commission, lower first (README: average, inverted); (3) validator age in epochs with non-zero vote credits, older first; (4) vote-credit ratio. The final score is this raw score multiplied by every binary gate, so one failed gate gives zero and the validator is ineligible. JIP-25 introduced this order in place of vote-credit ranking; it was posted 2025-08-20 and its author reported it executed through Realms in a post dated 2025-10-15.

Marinade Native (launched 2023-07-19) delegates SOL directly to over 100 validators. The user grants stake authority but keeps withdrawal authority, no mSOL is minted, and there is no performance fee. Marinade held over 7.2M SOL across Native and mSOL by August 2023.

Splitting an active or activating stake account needs a pre-funded destination and leaves both the source's remaining delegation and the destination's delegation at or above the minimum delegation (1 SOL). The destination inherits the source's activation and deactivation epochs, so a split never restarts warmup or cooldown. A fully inactive account splits freely as long as both halves stay rent-exempt.

Inflation rewards are paid on the effective portion of the stake for each epoch, and an epoch's rewards exist only after that epoch ends. A stake delegated in epoch N and fully effective from N+1 therefore earns its first reward for epoch N+1, credited at the start of epoch N+2. Rewards are added to the stake account's delegation (auto-compounding), so withdrawing earned rewards generally needs a deactivation first.

An LST's redemption rate is the SOL held by its stake pool divided by the LST supply. Kamino writes it as SOL_staked / LST_minted. The Steward's instant-unstake triggers include voting on under 70% of expected slots, commission above 5% or MEV commission above 10%, governance blacklisting and an unacceptable merkle root upload authority, capped at 10% of the pool per epoch. The stake program classifies a stake account by (effective, activating, deactivating): (0,0,0) is Inactive; effective 0 with some activating or deactivating stake is ActivationEpoch; (>0,0,0) is FullyActive. Any other combination, meaning some effective stake plus some activating or deactivating stake, is transient, and Merge fails with MergeTransientStake ('stake account with transient stake cannot be merged').

Solido hit 'stake account with transient stake cannot be merged' after a large reserve amount activated over several epochs and a second stake account created in a later epoch could not be merged into the first. The fix limited the 'two activating accounts can merge' predicate to accounts with the same activation_epoch. The commit reproduces the failure on a local validator (about 250,000 SOL activates per epoch there) and only guesses at v1 cases; its '~4,000,000 SOL on mainnet' reserve is context, not a mainnet reproduction.

Rewards are paid on the effective portion only. Points for an epoch are the stake's effective amount in that epoch times the vote credits earned in it (Anza docs; SIMD-0391 describes the same loop). Activating stake earns nothing. In the deactivation epoch the whole stake still counts as effective (the stake-interface code returns effective = deactivating = the full amount), so it earns for that epoch. In later cooldown epochs only the not-yet-cooled remainder earns. Rewards compound into the delegated stake, so they cannot be withdrawn without deactivating.

A split from an active or activating source now needs a destination pre-funded with the rent-exempt reserve, and the source remainder and the destination must each hold at least the minimum delegation, which blocks unlimited instant deactivation by repeated splitting. Per-account allowance per epoch is proportional: change = (account_portion / cluster_portion) * (cluster_effective * rate). Activation uses the previous epoch's activating and effective stake; deactivation uses deactivating and effective. The result is capped at the account's own waiting amount. Integer math saturates on overflow ('fail-safe, not fail-open'). Chorus One independently describes the same dependence on new stake relative to stake already active.

Typical activation or deactivation time is about one epoch (solanavalidators.wiki, 2026-05-15) to 1-2 epochs (stake.fish). The 9% rate limit is described as not binding for typical stakers (wiki) and 'warmup limits are rare' (Neodyme). Anza says cooldown 'may take several epochs ... depending on active stake and the size of your stake'. Large simultaneous flows therefore take longer.

Sources written before the 25%-to-9% change, and some that never updated, still quote the old rate. Chorus One (Feb 2021) says up to 25% can warm up or cool down per epoch. The Neodyme single-stake-pool review (2023-08-08) says the limit 'is currently set to 25%'. Current stake-program source uses 9%. Treat any 25% figure as historical unless it is dated after the feature activation.

Each epoch the runtime computes stake rewards in the first block and then distributes them over M following blocks, where M = ceil(stake accounts / 4,096), capped at 10% of the epoch's slots. Delegate, Deactivate, Withdraw, Split and Merge sent in that window fail and must be retried after it ends. SIMD-0118 cites about 550,000 active stake accounts on mainnet, which by its 4,096 target is roughly 135 blocks (own arithmetic).

EigenLayer slashing is opt-in. AVSs group operators into Operator Sets with their own slashing conditions, and an operator must opt into each set. Operators allocate part of their delegated stake as Unique Stake that only one AVS can slash, which isolates cross-AVS risk. A staker is exposed only if their operator joins a slashable set.

Peg mechanism: if an LST trades below its stake-rate value, an arbitrageur buys it, delayed-unstakes at the pool rate and keeps the difference. Kamino states this assumption outright. The tip distribution program does not compute the staker split. Only the account's `merkle_root_upload_authority` can upload a merkle root, and only from the epoch after the account was created and only until the first claim lands. Every claim must be signed by the same authority and carry a merkle proof against the stored root. The split between validator, stakers and fee is therefore fixed when TipRouter operators build the tree. Anza's SIMD-0123 text calls this a third-party trust model: Jito 'cannot enforce perfect compliance', so stakers and Jito must audit operators.

Lido's 2024 ReGOOSE proposal by Hasu argued stETH should always stay an LST, become the leading collateral in restaking markets, and support Ethereum-aligned validator services (starting with preconfirmations) without adding risk for stETH holders. It did not rule out a future stETH-based LRT. The Snapshot vote ran 2024-05-16 to 2024-05-23, and its outcome was not read here.

Lido's ReGOOSE proposal (Hasu, 2024-05-10) argued that stETH should always stay an LST, become the top collateral in restaking markets so stakers can opt into more risk, and support validator services such as preconfirmations without extra risk to stETH holders (for example through a dedicated cover fund). It did not rule out a separate Lido LRT product. The Snapshot vote ended 2024-05-23 and its result was not found in the thread text.

Jito's FAQ says slashing 'does not really exist right now on Solana', while also saying the exchange rate could fall in extreme cases from slashing or smart-contract bugs. Third-party review sites cite slashing and smart-contract risk as caveats; no JitoSOL loss event was found.

On 2026-04-18 at 17:35 UTC an attacker released 116,500 rsETH (about $292M, roughly 18% of circulating supply) from Kelp's mainnet LayerZero OFT escrow. The attacker used a forged cross-chain packet that claimed to come from Unichain. Kelp ran a 1-of-1 verifier, with LayerZero Labs as the sole DVN. LayerZero's post-mortem calls the method RPC poisoning, not key theft, and preliminarily attributes it to Lazarus Group's TraderTraitor unit. Kelp paused its contracts 46 minutes after the drain. This was a bridge-verification failure, not AVS slashing and not an Ethereum consensus event.

Neodyme (2023) notes a newly created single stake pool cannot take deposits in a rate-limited epoch, because its pool stake is transient until fully activated. After it has activated once it stays activated, and users simply deposit one epoch later. Withdrawals are unaffected.

Agave 4.1 removed the deprecated per-delegation `warmupCooldownRate` field (deprecated since 1.16.7) from jsonParsed stake account output. Client schemas that still require it throw 'Expected a number, but received: undefined' (Ledger Live PR #20135, merged 2026-07-28). The rate is a protocol constant, exposed via solana_stake_interface::state::warmup_cooldown_rate().

A pool program that merges deposits into its own stake account must wait until that account is fully effective. Neodyme's single-pool review found that deposits revert while the pool stake is transient. That can only happen to a newly created pool in an epoch where the global cap binds; withdrawals still work and users can deposit one epoch later. Neodyme calls it an inherent stake-program limitation that affects every pool that merges stake directly.

Agave 4.1 removed the deprecated warmupCooldownRate field (deprecated since 1.16.7) from jsonParsed stake delegations. Clients that still require it fail account sync with 'StructError: At path: stake.delegation.warmupCooldownRate -- Expected a number, but received: undefined' (Ledger Live PR #20135, merged 2026-07-28). The rate is a protocol constant exposed as warmup_cooldown_rate() in the stake interface, and Ledger's own activation math hardcodes 0.09.

An LRT holder stacks risk layers that a plain LST holder does not. Both face Ethereum consensus-layer penalties, which reach holders through oracle-reported rebases. An LRT adds AVS slashing if the operator opts in, plus LRT-protocol smart-contract risk. Lido's ReGOOSE post says restaking adds extra slashing conditions and that EigenLayer and LRT yields depended on subsidies and points programs it called unsustainable.

Jito's user guide lists these restaker risks: slashing due to operator misbehaviour (which 'may or may not be turned on'), custom vault programs, vault admins changing fees, technical risk from new NCNs, NCNs ceasing operations, and liquidity and exit risk when selling a VRT. Kiln (2025-02-27) adds that a VRT may not redeem 1:1, that vault contract or governance flaws could cause loss, and that centralisation could follow if a few NCNs attract most restaked assets.

Review the whole bridge and custody stack, not only the token. Galaxy says a single verifier on Kelp's LayerZero setup had 'effective admin-level power over Aave's WETH markets', so risk review must cover every trust assumption in an asset's bridge and custody stack, and it expects tighter LTVs and more isolation-mode listings for LRTs. Rekt says every audit came back clean and the failed verification layer 'wasn't in any audit scope'. Sevim and Torres (arXiv 2604.03274) likewise call an LRT's multi-chain expansion 'a double-edged sword' because bridging adds bridge risk to restaking risk.

The 10 Oct 2025 dislocations of BNSOL, wBETH and USDe were chiefly a Binance mark-price failure, and they show the cost of valuing LST collateral from a thin venue book. Gauntlet lists the properties that decide how a slash propagates through an LRT: the withdrawal queue, rewards structure, NAV oracle or exchange-rate module, secondary-market liquidity relative to volume, and insurance mechanisms. It proposes a lending killswitch that freezes new borrows during unexplained dislocations, and phased or redistributed slashing. Galaxy adds that risk review must cover every trust assumption in the asset's bridge and custody stack, not only the collateral asset.

Lending venues exposed lenders to LRT risk very differently. Galaxy reports Aave allowed rsETH as E-Mode collateral for WETH at 93% LTV (up from 72%) in January 2026, against 72% at SparkLend and about 75% at Fluid, and that Morpho's isolated markets held only about $1M of rsETH exposure. In the 2024 ezETH event Gauntlet's Morpho vault saw insolvency only in the 0.86-LLTV ezETH market (10.96 WETH); the 0.77-LLTV market had 8 liquidations and no insolvency.

A consensus-layer penalty reaches an LST holder through the protocol's accounting. Lido's bunker mode pauses withdrawal requests during a prolonged negative rebase so that exiting holders cannot dodge the loss (Chaos Labs). An AVS slash cuts delegator shares at once, including shares in queued withdrawals (ELIP-002), and Gauntlet models it as an immediate loss of an LRT's underlying funds.

On 2026-08-06 ether.fi announced that it had removed all restaking exposure from weETH, making weETH a pure LST. Restaking moved to weETHs, a separate LRT built on Symbiotic. Blockhead reports the last structural EigenLayer tie, the EigenPod withdrawal credentials, is due to go by Q4 2026. It quotes CEO Mike Silagadze: 'There were no meaningful yield opportunities in restaking', and adds 'perceived risk from stakers'.

At launch EigenLayer burned slashed funds (ERC-20 strategies sent to a dead address, native ETH locked in EigenPods). ELIP-006 added Redistributable Operator Sets: the AVS sets a redistributionRecipient when it creates the set, the address cannot be changed later and can be any address, and these sets cannot use the EIGEN or native-ETH strategies. So a staker's LST-strategy shares in such a set can be moved to an address the AVS chose.

DefiLlama's protocol API returns three parallel daily arrays: tvl (USD), tokens (units per asset) and tokensInUsd (USD per asset). Dividing tokensInUsd by tokens gives an implied unit price for each asset. Comparing the unit series with the USD series separates real flows from price moves, which a USD-only chart cannot do.

A Jito vault cannot use a Token-2022 mint in practice. Offside Labs rated 'Vault with Token-2022 Mint is Unusable' Low and Jito acknowledged it. Certora's second report flagged inconsistent token-program validation (fixed by PR #175, merged 2024-12-16, which standardises on the original SPL token program), and Jito declined its extension-validation finding because 'Token2022 is no longer supported'. JIP-6 had already said Token-2022 support would not be available initially.

Under ELIP-006 a redistributing operator set fixes its redistributionRecipient at creation, and the address cannot change. Only ERC-20 strategies qualify, so EIGEN and native ETH are excluded; LSTs such as stETH are ERC-20s, though the spec does not name them. Operators opt in and carry a 'Redistributable' label. The spec describes no separate staker opt-in. It warns: 'If an Operator itself is compromised, it may stand-up its own AVS to steal user funds'. It names no redistribution-specific allocation delay or veto.

An LST holder bears Ethereum consensus-layer penalties. An LRT holder bears those plus AVS slashing for any slashable Operator Set the LRT's operators have joined, plus the LRT protocol's own contract, oracle and operator-selection risk. LlamaRisk calls this 'dual slashing exposure' for LRTs from the 2025-04-17 AVS slashing launch.

Solayer's design differs from Jito's: a user converts SOL to sSOL, the stake is delegated to Solayer-recommended validators, and the sSOL is then delegated to a Solana dApp (an 'endogenous AVS') that receives AVS wrapper tokens as proof of stake. The dApp gains stake-weighted block-space priority, holders earn Solana staking yield plus MEV yield, and the dApp earns a share of staking commission. Solayer currently chooses the validators; letting dApps choose them is described as a future goal.

Three Solana lenders have code or docs that price an LST from the on-chain pool rate rather than a DEX price. Kamino's docs say all its LSTs, including JitoSOL, mSOL and bSOL, use stake-rate pricing read from the stake pool account. Jupiter Lend's oracle program lists StakePool (SPL pools such as Jito) and MsolPool (Marinade) as rate sources and names mSOL/SOL and JITOSOL/SOL as provider feeds; it accepts prices up to 600 seconds old for user operations and 7,200 seconds for liquidations, and checks Pyth confidence (2% and 4% of price) only for Pyth feeds. marginfi-v2 has oracle setups PythLST

Steward scoring runs every 10 epochs using a 30-epoch lookback. Inputs named by the independent Chainflow write-up are voting performance, commission, MEV commission and superminority rank, drawn from vote accounts, tip-distribution accounts and gossip data. Severe underperformance or a commission rug triggers immediate unstake and redelegation instead of waiting for the next cycle.

Marinade runs three products, and mSOL is no longer the main one. mSOL is the liquid token. Marinade Native (launched 2023-07-19) is a set of native stake accounts where Marinade holds stake authority and the user keeps withdrawal authority, with no token and no performance fee. Marinade Select (launched 2025-06-05) is an institutional product on KYC-verified validators. Messari's Q2 2025 report has Native passing mSOL by TVL (5.30M vs 4.98M SOL), Select at about 845K SOL, and 11.1M SOL combined; DefiLlama's 2025-06-30 values sum to the same 11.1M. Solayer's flow differs from Jito's: a user converts SOL into sSOL (staked with Solayer-recommended validators), then delegates sSOL to a Solana dApp, an 'endogenous AVS', which receives an AVS wrapper token. The dApp gets stake-weighted quality of service (block-space priority) and a share of staking commission; holders earn staking yield plus MEV yield. dApps cannot yet choose the validators, which the docs call a future goal. Binance Research (2025-02-11) says the endogenous AVS launched on mainnet in 2024 Q3 with Bonk, AltLayer, SonicSVM and Hashkey.

Sanctum earns a recurring fee on partner LSTs and shares it with the LST operator. Sanctum's LST docs state the default model as 10 bps withdrawal fee and a 10% epoch fee split equally between operators and Sanctum. Sanctum's co-founder said in Sep 2025 that Sanctum charges an AUM fee split 50/50 with partners such as Jupiter, Drift and Bybit, and also earns router fees, Reserve unstake fees and Infinity fees. Jupiter's docs describe a 5% Sanctum epoch fee on JupSOL base rewards split 2.5% to Sanctum and 2.5% to the Jupiter DAO treasury, which differs from the 10% default.

Since SIMD-0096 took effect in early 2025 the block leader keeps 100% of priority fees instead of 50%. No protocol rule passes any of it to stakers, so sharing is voluntary and happens outside the core protocol. Validators have sent part of it to their own liquid staking tokens, which helps only that LST's holders, or to NFT holders as the Cogent validator does. Ben Hawkins wrote in Oct 2024 that LST top-ups cannot reach the many stakers who stake natively.

Merge also needs matching Authorized values and Lockups that are identical or no longer in force, or it fails with MergeMismatch. When both accounts hold active stake, they must delegate to the same vote account and both must have deactivation_epoch = u64::MAX (neither deactivating), or Merge fails with MergeMismatch; activation epochs may differ. A FullyActive merge sets credits_observed to the stake-weighted average and moves the source's rent-exempt reserve to the destination as withdrawable lamports instead of staking it.

A stake delegated in epoch N earns nothing in N. If the cap does not bind it is fully effective from epoch N+1 and earns for N+1. Those rewards are computed at the N+1 to N+2 boundary and paid over the first blocks of N+2: SIMD-0118 targets 4,096 stake-account rewards per block instead of paying all at the first block. The slot within epoch N at which the delegation lands makes no difference, because activation_epoch is the epoch number only. The Solana Validators Wiki gives a worked case: confirmed in epoch 971, effective in 972, first reward paid in the first ~150 slots of 973.

marginfi's pool-rate pricing carries guards and a built-in lag. The pool account key must match the bank's configured oracle key and be owned by the SPL stake-pool program or one of two Sanctum forks. Supply must be above zero (ZeroSupplyInStakePool). The rate must lie between 0 and 3 (MAX_LST_SOL_RATE, a guard against garbage reads rather than donations). The pool may trail the current epoch by at most one (clock.epoch - last_update_epoch <= 1, else StakePoolStale). Operators receive delegated stake but have no direct control of it, and each vault decides how much stake each operator gets. Rewards accrue to the vault, so the VRT price rises instead of rewards being paid out separately. The NCN's registry entry stores no detailed config: accepted tokens, quorum and slashing conditions live in the NCN's own program. In the TipRouter and the default Template NCN, voting weight is frozen in a snapshot at the start of each consensus cycle, so stake moved mid-cycle cannot change voting power; the docs say other NCNs may define different snapshot mechanisms.

SIMD-0391 (Anza, created 2025-10-23, header status Activated) replaces f64 warmup and cooldown arithmetic with integer arithmetic: RATE_BPS = 900, u128 saturating multiplication, division last, result clamped to the account's own portion, minimum 1 lamport per epoch (not applied to reward payouts). It exists because eBPF forbids floating point. The stake interface 3.2.0 and later deprecate the float functions in favour of *_v2 versions, and stake program 5.1.0 uses stake_v2. Stake is far from uniform. In the researcher's decode the largest validator holds 14.03% of the pool (1,439,843 SOL), the top three 18.9%, the top 10 21.0%, the top 50 32.8% and the top 100 47.5%. Most of the rest sit near 30,000 SOL: 201 validators hold 30,000-60,000 SOL and 79 hold 10,000-30,000 SOL. The inverse Herfindahl index gives an effective number of about 43 validators (researcher's calculation). JIP-39 calls JitoSOL 'the most decentralised LST', a claim that rests on validator count rather than stake shares.

Pectra makes isolated slashing cheaper but shifts risk to correlated events. Chaos Labs models an isolated slashing on about 8,192 ETH of Lido stake at 22.48 ETH after Pectra versus 270.55 ETH before (down 91.7%). LlamaRisk warns that a consolidated 2,048 ETH validator can lose up to 64 times what a 32 ETH validator loses, and that correlation penalties could become much more severe when a few large validators are slashed together.

Operators receive delegated stake from vaults but do not control it, and each vault decides how much stake each operator receives. Vault rewards accrue to the vault, so the VRT price rises as rewards build rather than rewards being paid out separately.

Tips' share of staker yield has fallen sharply: Solana Compass reports about 10.3% total yield in Jan 2025 with 3.1 points from MEV tips (~30%), versus 5.0% in late Sep 2026 with 0.15 points from tips (~3%). A Jito-affiliated author estimated in Jan 2025 that tips raised staking rewards roughly 25-50%. Compass averages exclude validators that pay nothing, so 100%-commission validators are not counted.

The Nov 2022 drain showed the failure mode of a capped exit fee. Once the market discount exceeded the 3% maximum fee, every SOL added to Marinade's unstake pool was taken immediately at 3%, so liquidity providers earned a bounded fee while the pool stayed empty. A proposal sought a 9% maximum (the May 2023 settings show 9%); a forum participant reading the Flipside data called 9-10% reasonable because discounts near 10% were bought back quickly. Jito and Solayer sell different things. Jito's NCN framework serves arbitrary proof-of-stake services such as oracles, DePINs, bridges, whole chains or reward distribution, and each NCN defines its own consensus, rewards and (in future) slashing. Solayer's endoAVS is a Solana dApp that buys stake-weighted block-space priority with delegated sSOL, and Solayer chooses the validators. A 2024 third-party post drew the same split and called its view of Jito a guess.

Steward also gates on the Jito client stack, which is what produces MEV commission data. Eligible validators must be connected to BAM for at least 6 of the last 10 epochs (live config: jito_bam_minimum_epochs 6, jito_bam_window_epochs 10), and JIP-39 adds that validators not running BAM must run another Jito client such as FireBAM or jito-agave. Missing BAM data lowers the threshold rather than failing the validator.

Minimum delegation is a runtime value, read with the getStakeMinimumDelegation RPC method rather than a fixed constant. A live mainnet call on 2026-11-06 returned 1,000,000,000 lamports (1 SOL). Neodyme (2023) also says 1 SOL. The v1.14 stake program changes (forum.solana.com, May 2023) introduced the instruction and grandfathered existing smaller stakes, which may still deactivate or merge into a larger stake.

SIMD-0490 makes the stake program read rent from the Rent sysvar instead of Meta.rent_exempt_reserve. New accounts still record rent_exempt_reserve = 2,282,880 lamports (the reserve for a 200-byte stake account) for compatibility, and Withdraw and Split compute the rent minimum from the Rent sysvar.

Sevim and Torres report that on 2025-10-09 about $19.23B was restaked, roughly 13% of the 35.7M ETH staked, of which $13.97B was native restaking and $4.06B liquid restaking. ether.fi's eETH held 65.4% of all LRTs, so the LRT market was concentrated in one issuer. The DefiLlama category table in the same paper lists ether.fi at $11.21B, so category definitions differ from the paper's own count.

Jito targets external, arbitrary proof-of-stake services (NCNs such as oracles, bridges, DePIN and the Tip Router that distributes MEV tips), whereas Solayer's first stage targets applications inside Solana. A third-party 2024 blog framed this split but called its view of Jito 'speculation'.

The same oracle trade-off appears on Ethereum. In June 2023 BGD Labs (an Aave service provider) replied to Gauntlet's LST 'killswitch' plan that exchange-rate pricing assumes the primary rate is the fair price: if the peg does not recover for months, that assumption is broken. BGD said a real risk of permanent depeg should mean not listing the LST (LT of 0), not a 93% or 97% threshold, and that raising borrow rates or lowering LT during a secondary-market depeg hurts users without making liquidation more attractive.

As of 2026-11-06 an epoch lasts about 26 hours, not the 2 to 3 days older sources quote. Anza's announcement of the 200 ms step said 'An epoch now takes about a day instead of two', and Solana Compass estimated roughly 26 hours once the 15-19 ms overshoot seen at earlier steps is included. This pass measured 25.5 to 25.7 hours per epoch (about 212-214 ms per slot) from getBlockTime at the first slot of epochs 1064, 1068, 1072, 1076, 1077 and 1078 on public mainnet RPC. Epoch 1078 began 2026-11-05 11:54:47 UTC. An unstake that waits for one boundary therefore waits at most about a day.

Community monitoring exists for the redistributable-slashing risk. A user in the EigenYields thread published a Dune dashboard and a scanner repository (2026-09-06) that compute slashed totals directly from SlashExecuted events instead of trusting operator claims, and flag operators with a 0-day allocation delay and tiny AVS membership. The repository link given in the thread returned HTTP 404 when fetched, so the scanner itself was not inspected.

Skepticism predates both launches. CoinDesk (2024-05-01) quoted Blockworks Research's Ryan Connor saying Solana has 'far less of a need' for restaking than Ethereum because it is 'integrated' rather than 'modular'. At that point Picasso ran Solana's only working restaking product, with about $8M deposited.

Activating, deactivating and partially active accounts are rejected. The source must keep at least the minimum delegation or give up everything. MoveLamports moves only excess lamports. After the JIP-16 priority-fee rollout, a merkle root calculation discrepancy overstated claimable amounts under specific conditions involving validator MEV commission rates.
